newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds made up for last week's poor performance, spurred on by Germany, but outstripping bund gains by the close, dealers said.
"It was a small recovery from last week's underperformance of 10-year guilders," one trader said.
The new Dutch 10-year benchmark, the 5.75 percent February 2007 paper, gained 0.21 points to 101.70/80 for a bid yield of 5.52 percent. The spread under bunds widened by two basis points to 9 bp.
Payment is due for the new bonds on February 18 and some traders said this had probably helped usher the paper up.
"If you have a short in them, you have to pay, so we're probably seeing some short covering," one dealers said.
Dealers said traded volume in the issue topped a billion.
The longer-dated strength came partly at the expense of shorter maturity issues which were broadly unchanged. July 6.25 percent 1998s, for example, closed down 0.01 points.
Traders said a number of professionals were keen to lengthen their positions, having noticed that some issues were becoming expensive.
"There's been lots of outright buying today, and selling of shorts," one trader said.
